children: gained 1.4% in Friday's trading as Bernstein upgraded shares to Market Perform from Underperform with a $171 price target, raised from $145, reflecting a "refreshed understanding" of the company's transformation following a recent meeting with management.
Bernstein analyst Varun Govindaraj said he now believes 3M
has been structurally transformed through an "R&D factory" approach that manages product commercialization like a portfolio, with pipeline reviews, data, and an ROI focus for capital deployment.

Previous issues that affected R&D effectiveness—PFAS replacement, fewer but bigger bets, healthcare draining capital—no longer impact the organization going forward, the analyst said, largely driving his improved organic growth forecast for 3M
to 3.5%-4% from ~3% in his discounted cash flow model.

is in the early stages of a short-cycle recovery, likely driven by AI capex, that should last for another couple of years, and as "the quintessential short-cycle business, 3M has a secular tailwind from this."
The analyst thinks PFAS is less of a risk than previously thought, seeing 3M

as well-positioned to absorb any incremental negative news; the company is in negotiations with plaintiffs on personal injury lawsuits rather than going through a bellwether case process, which is a "positive sign" and could largely eliminate previous concerns over a multi-year overhang.
ability to reach ~25% operating margins in 2026 with gross margins gradually rising to the mid-40s and possibly higher over the back half of this decade.

title: 3M upgraded at Bernstein on R&D structural change, less PFAS risk than expected
